newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end lower on sliding beef prices.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end lower on sliding beef prices.

text.p: Another drop in boxed beef prices at midday weighed on CME live cattle futures and prices ended lower, traders said. Feeder cattle reacted to price swings in corn before finishing mostly lower as corn values climbed late, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.500 to 0.050 cent per lb lower with April off most at 68.325 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.025 cent higher to 0.550 lower with May off 0.325 at 68.600 cents.
Further decline in wholesale beef values pressure futures from the start as did a weaker tone to cash cattle prices as the day unfolded, traders said.

"(Packers) took so much out of the beef that it started to worry the industry and (feedlots) did trade a few cattle down at $67 in the Panhandle - $1 lower on a modest trade," said Chuck Levitt, senior livstock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
Heavy-weight choice boxed beef prices fell another $0.94 per cwt at noon to $101.90, down $6.09 since the recent high set on March 4 and the lowest level since February 24.

Spreaders bought April and sold June early but the "Goldman roll", rolling of long April positions into June by the Goldman Sachs fund, weighed on April late. Large open interest in April added to bearish sentiment, traders said.
Ideas on Friday's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report lightly weighed on back months. The report is expected to show large February feedlot placements and much-larger-than-year-ago on-feed supplies.

Analyst estimates ranged from 105 to 107.5 percent of a year ago for on-feed supplies at the seven major cattle feeding states as of March 1 and averaged 106.5 percent. February placement estimates averaged 104.2 percent of a year earlier in a range of 99 to 110 percent and marketings averaged 97.9 in a a range of 94 to 99 percent.
Refco spread long April/short June after selling both early. R.J. O'Brien April early, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, trading remained light with small commercial hedging late, buying June puts and selling caslls. Commission houses bought April 70 calls early. Volatility was steady to firm, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures followed CBOT corn futures price swings in an inverse fashion and ended lower after corn futures turned higher, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.04 at $68.65 per cwt.
ADM Investor Services sold May late and RBH notably sold early, pit sources said.
